speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing issues with your gait and coordination; could you please describe when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting progressively worse? Also, do you have a history of alcohol use or any family history of similar neurological conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The asymmetry of your symptoms, specifically the clumsiness on the right side, is a crucial detail that suggests a focal issue rather than a systemic one like alcohol use or genetic ataxia. Have you experienced any recent head trauma, or do you have a history of conditions such as multiple sclerosis, stroke, or brain tumors?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Natalizumab carries a known risk for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), which aligns with your focal neurological symptoms. Have you experienced any recent changes in your vision, speech difficulties, or cognitive confusion?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.
